data.name: Faqeer
data.gender_notes: Faqeer is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who is in need of Allah, deprived, humble, and reliant upon Allah. The name Faqeer carries the meaning “Poor, needy, mendicant” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu. Parents who choose Faqeer usually hope their child will grow to embody poor, needy, mendicant and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_arabic.name: فقير
in_arabic.meaning: من هو الفقير؟ فقير هو الشخص الفقير أو المتعفف
in_arabic.long_meaning: الفقير هو الشخص الذي يعيش في فقر أو هو الشخص المتعفف الذي لا يطلب من الناس شيئاً، و في اللغة العربية، اشتقت كلمة فقير من الفقر، و هو ضد الغنى. وردت كلمة فقير في القرآن الكريم عدة مرات، منها قوله تعالى: {وَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِيَ كِتَابَهُ بِشِمَالِهِ فَيَقُولُ يَا لَيْتَنِي لَمْ أُؤْتَ كِتَابِيهْ * وَلَمْ أَدْرِ مَا حِسَابِيهْ * يَا لَيْتَهَا كَانَتِ الْقَضِيَّةُ مَوْتِي قَبْلَ أَنْ أُؤْتَى هَذَا * وَمَا أَدْرَانِي مَا حِسَابِيهْ * لَوْ أَنَّهَا كَانَتِ الْأَغْرَاضُ لَم أَسَأْ تَضَمَّنَ الْخَطِيئَهْ}

in_urdu.name: فقیر
in_urdu.meaning: فقیر کا مطلب ہے وہ شخص جو غریب ہے یا خود کو غریب سمجھتا ہے
in_urdu.long_meaning: فقیر وہ شخص ہوتا ہے جو فقر یا تنگدستی میں جیتا ہے یا وہ شخص جو اپنی زندگی میں سادگی اختیار کرتا ہے اور لوگوں سے کچھ نہیں مانگتا۔ اردو میں فقیر کا لفظ عربی زبان سے ماخوذ ہے، جہاں اس کا مطلب ہے 'غریب' یا 'سادہ زندگی گذرانے والا'۔ فقیر کا ذکر اردو شاعری اور تصوف میں بھی کیا گیا ہے، جہاں اس کا استعمال روحانی سفر پر چلنے والے سادہ لوحی فرد کے لیے کیا جاتا ہے

in_hindi.name: फ़क़ीर
in_hindi.meaning: फ़क़ीर का अर्थ है कोई व्यक्ति जो दरिद्री या निर्धन है
in_hindi.long_meaning: फ़क़ीर वह व्यक्ति होता है जो दरिद्री या निर्धनता में जीवन व्यतीत करता है, या वह व्यक्ति जो सादगी से जीवन यापन करता है और लोगों से कुछ नहीं मांगता। फ़क़ीर शब्द का उपयोग हिंदू धर्म और इस्लाम दोनों में किया जाता है, जहां यह शब्द आध्यात्मिक यात्रा पर चलने वाले व्यक्ति के लिए उपयोग किया जाता है जो सांसारिक संपत्ति और विलास से दूर रहता है

in_pashto.name: فقیر
in_pashto.meaning: فقیر د بې وزلي سړی یا هغه چا چې په بې وزلۍ کې ژوند کوي
in_pashto.long_meaning: فقیر هغه سړی دی چې په فقر یا بې وزلۍ کې ژوند کوي، یا هغه سړی دی چی د خپل ژوند لپاره سادگي غوره کوي او له نورو څخه څه نه غواړي. په پښتو کلتور کې، فقیر اکثرا د صوفی عارف یا هغه چا په توګه کارول کیږي چې د روحاني سفر پر مخ دي

in_english.name: Faqeer
in_english.meaning: A person who is poor or lives a simple life
in_english.long_meaning: A Faqeer is an individual who lives a life of poverty, simplicity, and often spiritual devotion. The term originates from Arabic roots, specifically 'fa-qar', meaning 'to be poor or needy'. In Islamic tradition, a Faqeer may refer to a Sufi ascetic who renounces worldly possessions and desires. The term Faqeer appears in the Quran and Hadith, highlighting the virtues of humility, piety, and reliance on God. In modern times, the term is used across Muslim cultures to describe someone who lives modestly and humbly

data.cultural_impact: The term "Faqeer" is derived from the Arabic root "faqara", which means "to become poor" or "to be deprived". Historically, the Faqeer were wandering Sufi dervishes who lived a simple life, often begging for alms from the local population in the hopes of attaining spiritual enlightenment. Through their humble demeanor and reliance on Allah, they inspired a deep sense of reverence and respect in the communities they visited. The Faqeer's embodiment of selfless devotion and commitment to the spiritual path continue to influence Islamic culture to this day, particularly in the Middle East and South Asia.
data.spiritual_significance: The term "Faqeer" carries a profound spiritual significance as it represents one who is completely surrendered to Allah and recognizes their utter dependence on the divine. The Faqeer's humility and detachment from worldly possessions highlight the importance of inner purification and the pursuit of knowledge and wisdom in the Islamic tradition. Moreover, the term speaks to the universal human experience of vulnerability and need for divine guidance, making it a powerful reminder of the transcendent reality that lies beyond the material realm.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The meaning "Poor, needy, mendicant" symbolizes One who is in need of Allah, deprived, humble, and reliant upon Allah. In Islamic spirituality, bearing the name Faqeer serves as a constant reminder of one's spiritual aspirations and connection to Islamic values of poor, needy, mendicant.

islamic_reference.note: Traditional Islamic name with deep spiritual significance in Islamic culture

historical_references.reference: The Sufi Order of the Chishtis, founded around 1006 AD in present-day Pakistan, named their disciples as 'Faqeer' or 'Fakir'. The term signified a wandering dervish, seeking spiritual enlightenment through poverty and humility.

The Persian poet Rumi (1207-1273 AD) used the term 'Faqir' in his poetry to denote a poor, humble seeker of God. He emphasized the importance of detachment from worldly possessions for spiritual growth.

modern_usage.modern_context: The Islamic term 'Faqeer' or 'Fakir', which originally referred to a penniless, destitute person, has taken on new meanings in modern contexts. In spiritual terms, it is often used to describe an individual who recognizes their spiritual poverty and seeks to fill that void through devotion and submission to Allah. This concept is particularly popular on social media platforms, where individuals use the label 'Faqeer' to express feelings of self-deprecation and humility. In literature and poetry, the Faqeer is a common archetype, often portrayed as a wandering dervish seeking enlightenment. In Sufi circles, the Faqeer is a spiritual guide or mentor, helping others on their journey towards self-realization and closeness to Allah.
